Deposit insurance: leave room for interest as well as principal

Four graphics explain one-name deposit aggregation, separate member limits and how hypothetical retained interest can use coverage headroom.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 4 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Explore one-name deposit coverage and interest headroom

CDIC one-name category illustration for one individual across both members, using the CAD 100,000 principal-plus-interest limit reviewed 25 October 2026. Both member labels are hypothetical, assumed to be distinct CDIC member institutions. Member A balances are aggregated in the same category; include all eligible deposits and accrued interest in that category, not only one account or brand. Eligibility, actual issuer/member identity and ownership records are not verified. All balances earn the same hypothetical constant effective annual interest, retained and compounded, with no new deposits, withdrawals, tax payments or fees. The current limit is held constant for sensitivity analysis, not forecast as future policy. Other coverage categories, trust/broker/nominee arrangements, foreign-currency valuation and provincial insurance schemes are excluded. Amounts above a modeled cap are unprotected by this assumed coverage, not a predicted loss; insurance also does not make a deposit accessible before maturity.

The central idea

Identify the eligible deposits, category and actual member institution first. Then include accrued interest when comparing the combined amount with the applicable cap.

01

Use the member and category as the coverage unit

CDIC’s coverage overview states that eligible deposits are insured up to CAD 100,000, including principal and interest, in each covered category at a member institution. Eligibility matters: a balance is not insured simply because it appears on a financial account statement.

This guide restricts the illustration to deposits held in one name by the same individual across both members. CDIC explains that eligible savings, chequing and term deposits in that category are combined. Opening a second account within the same member and category does not provide a second CAD 100,000 cap.

Member A and member B are hypothetical and assumed genuinely distinct. Use the official member list to check the relevant institution and trade name. A branch or brand label alone is not enough evidence for the model’s separate-member assumption.

02

Aggregate the starting balances before testing the limit

The example has CAD 60,000 of eligible savings and CAD 30,000 of other eligible one-name deposits at member A. Together they make CAD 90,000, leaving CAD 10,000 of headroom under the illustrated cap.

Member B has CAD 50,000 in the same one-name category. Because B is assumed to be a separate CDIC member, its balance is tested against its own cap. The example therefore starts with CAD 140,000 within the two assumed coverage limits.

Include all eligible amounts in the same member/category, not just the deposit currently being considered. Starting figures should already reflect interest accrued up to that date. The model grows only subsequent interest; it does not reconstruct missing account records or verify eligibility.

03

Retained interest can take a balance above the cap

The default assumes a constant 4% effective annual rate for five years, with all interest retained and compounded. This is a hypothetical rate, not an available offer. There are no new deposits, withdrawals, tax payments or fees.

Member A’s CAD 90,000 grows to CAD 109,498.76. Applying the same assumed CAD 100,000 cap leaves CAD 9,498.76 above it. Member B’s CAD 50,000 grows to CAD 60,832.65 and remains below its own cap.

Combined projected balances are about CAD 170,331.41, of which CAD 160,832.65 is within the modeled caps. The interest chart shows A starting below the cap and exceeding it by year three under these assumptions. That does not forecast an actual deposit yield or a future change in insurance rules.

04

Treat interest headroom as a sensitivity calculation

Under a fixed cap and constant compounded rate, a starting amount that grows exactly to the cap is cap ÷ (1 + annual rate)years. At 4% for five years, that is about CAD 82,192.71 for a CAD 100,000 cap.

This is arithmetic for the stated assumptions, not a universal deposit allocation. Actual interest-crediting terms, other eligible deposits, ownership records, accrued amounts and future rules can change the comparison. Money withdrawn to pay tax would also change the balance path, but no such withdrawal is assumed here.

The matrix varies the interest assumption and horizon while keeping starting balances and member classification selected. Unused headroom at B is not subtracted from an excess at A. Each member/category is tested separately before the excesses are added.

05

Keep coverage, liquidity and investment risk as separate questions

An amount above the modeled cap is not a predicted loss. It is an amount this illustration does not count as insured under its assumptions. CDIC protection concerns eligible deposits if a member fails; it does not make a locked-in deposit accessible whenever a bill arrives.

The coverage overview also distinguishes eligible deposits from products such as mutual funds, shares and ETFs. A product’s account wrapper does not replace the need to identify what is held.

For a review, record the actual member, ownership category, all eligible balances and accrued interest, then check the payment or maturity dates separately. Other categories and provincial insurance schemes require their own rules; this single-category example does not calculate them.

Sources and scope

Public sources reviewed on 25 October 2026. These graphics apply the current CDIC one-name limit to hypothetical eligible balances and interest assumptions. They do not verify a real member, account classification or future insurance decision. The worked examples, scenario assumptions, and research checklists are TickerLantern’s own educational analysis; they are not source-reported investment results. Recheck current issuer documents for any product-specific decision.
